subject: ventures/earthwork-cut-fill
professional: a senior civil estimator / grading contractor who prices pad and site earthwork from a surveyor's point file; first checks: ft3 to yd3 divided by 27, mixed cut/fill triangles split on the daylight line rather than netted, shrink applied to cut becoming compacted fill and swell to the bank volume that is trucked, the balance elevation, topsoil strip, and whether pad side slopes and mass haul are in or out

evidence.correctness: Recomputed by hand from textbook formulas the author did not write (`node /tmp/claude-0/audit-earthwork/recompute.mjs`, `fourpoint.mjs`). (A) planar ground z=100+0.05x on a 100x100 ft lot, flat pad 102.5: daylight at x=50; by average-end-area with sections at x=0,25,50 (fill end areas 250,125,0 sq ft x 100 ft) fill = 25(250+125)/2 + 25(125+0)/2 = 6,250 ft3 = 231.481 yd3, cut the same: tool 231.4815/231.4815. (B) balance with 20% shrink on the same ground: 0.8*100(10a^2-100a+250) = 1000a^2 gives a^2+40a-100=0, a=2.36068, E=102.36068: tool 102.36069. (C) mixed-cell triangle (0,0),(30,0),(0,30), depths +3,-1,-1: fill = A d1^3/(3(d1-d2)(d1-d3)) = 450*27/48 = 253.125 ft3 = 9.375 yd3, net A*1/3 = 150 so cut 103.125 ft3 = 3.819 yd3: tool 3.8194/9.375. (D,E) Caterpillar Performance Handbook convention CCY = BCY(1-shrink), LCY = BCY(1+swell): cut 1000/fill 700/15%/25%/12 cy: export bank 1000-700/0.85 = 176.47, loose 220.59, 19 loads; cut 500/fill 700: import bank 275/0.85 = 323.53, loose 404.41, 34 loads: all match. (G) 0.5 ft strip on A: fill 9,000 ft3 = 333.33, cut 4,000 = 148.15, strip 185.19 yd3: match. (F) metres: 6,250 m3 (no /27): match. Four-point (borrow-pit) on one 50x50 non-planar cell (100,102,104,101; pad 98): A*sum/4 = 9,375 ft3; the TIN gives 9,583.33, which is exactly the SW-NE diagonal split (the other diagonal gives 9,166.67, the mean is the borrow-pit value), the expected method difference, not an error. check/differential.py rerun: identical triangle sets to SciPy Qhull on five 800-point state-plane sets, volumes to 6.04e-14. Not a 4: a space- or tab-delimited point file with a comma in a description ('EP, CURB') is split on the comma and the shot dropped, silently if it is the first line.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features run end to end: header/PNEZD/PENZD/NEZ/ENZ parsing (works; comma-in-description caveat), duplicate positions reported, Delaunay TIN (Qhull-identical), max-edge, plane and two-TIN designs (tests), boundary either winding with uncovered share warned, topsoil strip, shrink, swell, trucks, balance elevation, CSV summary, plan map (index.html:213-229 read), CLI (`node cli.mjs --example --balance --shrink 15` prints balanced pad 109.193 ft, 921.7 cut / 783.5 fill = 921.7*0.85). Explainer worked example matches CLI (page.test.mjs passes). Breaklines, daylight slopes, LandXML and mass haul are listed under Next, not claimed. One dead block (earthwork.mjs:567-569). No TODOs or stubs.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/earthwork-cut-fill && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 30 tests, 30 pass, 1.7 s. check/differential.py reproduced (output identical to check/RESULT.txt). Nine mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: swell applied to compacted instead of bank caught; import bank without /keep caught; zero-depth vertex dropped from the cut side caught; trucks ceil->round caught; strip sign flipped caught; perVolume 27->26 caught; perVolume 27->27.0001 survived (4e-6 relative, below any tolerance that matters); the 'balanced' tolerance widened 100x (0.5 yd3/0.01% -> 5 yd3/1%) survived; bisection capped at 13 iterations survived. Tests are closed-form and author-derived but backed by an external differential against Qhull.
evidence.craft: Read earthwork.mjs (about 640 lines), cli.mjs, index.html script, check/*. Pure functions, origin-shifted Bowyer-Watson, exact polygon integration, textContent-only DOM writes, num() maps a blank field to null and the page then errors on a blank pad. Defects: splitLine tests for ',' before tab or whitespace (earthwork.mjs:33), so a delimiter inside a description re-splits the row; the first unparseable row is silently taken as a header even when it holds numbers (earthwork.mjs:86); dead `if (input.maxEdge ...) {}` block (earthwork.mjs:567); CLI Number('abc') -> NaN then `|| 0` silently zeroes shrink/swell (cli.mjs:22, earthwork.mjs:571); run() does not range-check shrink (shrink 150 -> bank Infinity rendered as the infinity sign; page max=90 is advisory only).
evidence.claims: Checked against files: TIN method, exact split, PNEZD default, Qhull differential (check/RESULT.txt backs 'to 1e-13' in llms.txt and '6e-14' in README), worked example (page.test.mjs), disclaimer (index.html footer, README, explainer), made-up example labelled. Live https://marisstella.app/earthwork-cut-fill/ returned 200 with canonical on marisstella.app; llms.txt served with marisstella.app origins. Not backed: (a) the FAQ 'Is my survey uploaded?' answer and its JSON-LD copy say 'Nothing is sent anywhere' (index.html:151, :12), but the served page loads ../pf-site.js, which sends a navigator.sendBeacon page-view hit (slug, plus ref/referrer source) to a workers.dev counter (platform/pages/build.mjs:10484); the survey itself is not sent, and the footer checkbox does not silence that beacon (it honours DNT/GPC and portfolio-hub-optout only); (b) README.md:52 says earthwork.test.mjs has 22 tests, it has 21.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: paste a 154-shot point file, set a boundary, find the balance pad with 15% shrink, read export/import and truckloads, download the CSV. Works in seconds. A grading contractor pricing a building pad hits in the first hour: no daylight side slopes (the 2:1 or 3:1 fill and cut slopes outside the pad are often a large share of the dirt and can only be had by hand-building a proposed TIN), no breaklines (curbs and ditches cut across), one shrink for both site cut and import borrow, no separate topsoil respread/export in the balance, and no mass-haul or haul-distance view. All but the borrow-shrink point are disclosed in Limits/Next.
evidence.domain: Compared against TIN-to-TIN volume surfaces (as in Civil 3D/Carlson), the average-end-area and four-point borrow-pit methods (FHWA/state DOT earthwork practice) and the Caterpillar Performance Handbook bank/loose/compacted convention. Matches: /27, exact daylight split, shrink on cut-to-compacted, swell on the bank volume hauled, balance on cut(1-shrink)=fill, strip lowering existing before computing. Departs: import borrow assumed to share the site's shrink (code comment only, earthwork.mjs:469, not on the page); 'balanced' declared within 0.5 yd3 or 0.01% (fine) but untested; no side slopes or mass haul (disclosed).

FAQ and FAQPage JSON-LD say 'Nothing is sent anywhere', but the served page's pf-site.js sends a page-view beacon (slug, ref/referrer source) to a workers.dev counter, and the footer opt-out checkbox does not stop it; no survey data is sent

verdict: Below the bar on claims only, and close. The volume engine is right: eight hand recomputations (average-end-area wedge, balance quadratic with 20% shrink, a mixed cut/fill triangle in closed form, Caterpillar-convention export and import with swell and trucks, topsoil strip, metric units, and a four-point borrow-pit cell that the TIN brackets exactly) all match, the Qhull differential reproduces to 6e-14, 30 tests pass and 6 of 9 seeded mutants are caught. A grading estimator's first checks (/27, mixed cells split not netted, shrink on cut-to-fill, swell on hauled bank) all pass. What holds it back: the privacy FAQ says nothing is sent while the served page beacons a page view; a comma inside a description in a tab or space file drops a shot, silently when it is the first row; and a real pad bid needs daylight slopes and a separate borrow shrink, which are not modelled (slopes are disclosed).
